In this vignette we will go through the process of identifying cell-wise epigenetic potential genes using single cell dataset. We start with two Single-cell datasets i.e. single cell atac-seq and single cell rna-seq. Both these datasets needs to be processed to get cell types. In case the cell-type annotation is not done/difficult for scATAC-seq, cell type labels can be transferred from scRNA-seq. There are multiple ways to do label transfer, we show one way of doing it using scglue pipeline in a separate jupyter notebook. 

```{r setup}
library(epiPot)
```


### Set path and environment

```{r environment, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source('epigenetic_potential_utilities.R')
# lung_case_path <- file.path(path, 'results','motif')
```

### Load pre-processed objects

In this vignette we assume that the user has single-cell datasets with cell-type annotations for both scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq. Another assumption here is that both datasets have some if not all cell types matching each other. (Note: make sure you dont have situation like cell types in scRNAseq has T-cell and scATAC-seq has T_cell or t_cell)

```{r load_objects, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
lung_rna <- read_rds('data/GSE161382/seurat_lung.rds')
signac_ig <- read_rds('data/GSE161381/signac_ig.rds')
```

### Main function call
Once the pre-requisite for calling the main epigenetic potential function we need to have following parameters \
1. Pair of count matrices from scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq in sparse format (default in Seurat) \
2. Cell type annotation vector of cells of scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq (In case you need to transfer labels from scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq or vice a versa please refer to the jupyter notebook) \
3. Sample vector for the cells \

```{r main_function, eval=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=TRUE}

# main workflow for cell-wise epigenetic potential
epigenetic_potential <- function(atac_counts, 
                                 atac_cell_types,
                                 atac_samples,
                                 rna_counts,
                                 rna_cell_types,
                                 rna_samples) {
  
  # create aggregate matrix from count matrix
  rna_aggr_mat <- matrix_aggregate(
    rna_counts, 
    rna_cell_types,
    rna_samples
  )
  atac_aggr_mat <- matrix_aggregate(
    atac_counts, 
    atac_cell_types,
    atac_samples
  )
  
  # Z-score scaling of the aggregate matrices
  rna_zr <- data.frame(t(scale(t(rna_aggr_mat))) )
  atac_zr <- data.frame(t(scale(t(atac_aggr_mat))) )
  
  # annotate peaks to genes for ATAC-seq
  atac_zr_anno <- annotate_peaks_pseudobulk(atac_zr)
  
  # create merged matrix of scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data
  merged_mat <- create_merged_matrix(atac_zr_anno, rna_zr)
  
  # create metadata for model matrix
  design_meta <- create_design_matrix(atac_zr_anno, rna_zr)
  
  # create model matrix
  model <- model.matrix(~ 0 + cell / tech, data = design_meta)
  
  # arrange columns as per model matrix
  merged_matrix <- merged_mat[, row.names(model)]
  
  # create limma model
  fit <- lmFit(merged_matrix, model)
  fit <- eBayes(fit)
  
  # parse limma results
  res <- parse_limma_res(fit)
  res
}

epipot <- epigenetic_potential(
  signac_ig@assays$peaks@counts,  # Sparse count matrix (scATAC-seq)
  signac_ig@meta.data$cell_type,  # Meta data column for cell-type (scATAC-seq)
  signac_ig@meta.data$orig.ident, # Meta data column for sample id (scATAC-seq)
  lung_rna@assays$RNA@counts,     # Sparse count matrix (scRNA-seq)
  lung_rna@meta.data$cells_short, # Meta data column for cell-type (scRNA-seq)
  lung_rna@meta.data$orig.ident)  # Meta data column for sample id (scRNA-seq)

epipot
```


### PROGENy enrichment analysis

#### functions in utilities

```{r progeny, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="50%"}

outpath <- file.path(path, 'results')
merged_sc <- 
  readRDS(file.path(path,'merged_sc_adults.rds'))
res <- readRDS(file.path(path, 'limma_res_adult.rds'))

progeny_res <- run_progeny(merged_sc, res)
ht_data <- plot_data(progeny_res)
dotplot_ord <- make_dotplot(ht_data,'Adult Lungs')
dotplot_ord <- dotplot_ord + theme(axis.text=element_text(size=12),
                  axis.title=element_text(size=14,face="bold"))
dotplot_ord
```
